steps.text: Sift flour, baking powder, and salt together in a medium bowl; set aside.
Beat sugar and butter in a large bowl with an electric mixer until smooth.
Beat first egg into butter mixture. Beat second egg into mixture along with vanilla extract; add flour mixture and stir until dough is just combined.
Wrap dough and chill in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease two cookie sheets.
Roll out dough on a clean floured surface to 1/4-inch thickness. Cut out shapes using Christmas cookie cutters; arrange them on the prepared cookie sheets. Gather scraps and repeat this step.
Bake in batches in the preheated oven until edges are golden, about 6 to 8 minutes. Cool on the baking sheet briefly before removing to a wire rack to cool completely before frosting or decorating.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Soft Christmas Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This Christmas cookie recipe makes soft, tender cut-out sugar cookies that hold their shape and are fun to decorate with colored sugar or icing for gifting.

video.description: Learn how to make an easy cookie dough, perfect for rolling out and cutting into your favorite shapes. With simple ingredients that you already have in your pantry (flour, margarine or butter, eggs, and flavorings) you can whip these up without a special trip to the grocery store.

review.reviewBody: WONDERFUL! For a perfect, soft sugar cookie, the following small modifications will get you there...use butter instead of marg, and melt it over the stove. It helps to dissolve the sugar, and to help sugars and butters cream better. Use only 3 cups flour. Finally, oven temp at 350 and baking cookies for 8-10 minutes keeps it soft. Lining with parchment paper also helps. Keep an eye out...they will seem too pale to remove from the oven, but just when the center doesn't look "wet" anymore, it is done. They still bake for 2 or so minutes, so they will darken up a little and be perfect. FYI--when rolling these out, keep the dough nice and thick...the cookie will be crisp (still good)if it is too thin.

FANTASTIC! I have made these MANY times now, and they are always well-received. I do make some recommended changes: butter instead of margarine, 3 1/3 cups flour and sub 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup powdered sugar for the 1 1/2 cups white sugar called for. I also use powdered sugar - as opposed to flour - when rolling them out. These are easy to handle, and hold up FABULOUSLY . . . tasting great even a week later! I use the Sugar Cookie Icing on this site, and they always look amazing. A side note: the first time I made these I made a batch of this recipe AND a batch of the Best Rolled Sugar Cookies, and these were by FAR better - both in texture and taste.

After many years of failed attempts at sugar cookies, I believed that it was just not in the stars for me to be a sugar cookie maker, I would just buy store made dough and decorate every year. :( To my surprise, I tried this recipe thinking it would turn out like the rest, (too floury, bland, or just plain gross) but they didn't...they were perfect! I used 1 stick salted and 1 stick unsalted butter, 1 c. white sugar/1 c. powdered sugar and left everything else the same. And chilled in fridge overnight. I also used powdered sugar to roll instead of flour (I did NOT want floury cookies!) Baked in conv. oven at 400 for 8-9 min, cooled on baking sheet for appx 1 min then cooled rest of way on rack. Crisp edge yet soft cookie. My husband says he never wants store bought dough again! Thanks for the great recipe!!!

I followed some of the other reviewers suggestions & changed the following: -Used 3 & 1/3 C. Flour -1 C. Salted Butter (Not margarine) -1 C. White Sugar + 1 C. Icing Sugar (Instead of 1 & 1/2 C. White Sugar) -Dusted the countertop with Icing Sugar (Instead of flour) -Baked at 350 for about 9 min Delicious!!! (Didn't even need frostig)

After reading through other suggestions in these comments I lowered the temp to 375 and baked for 7 minutes. They're definitely thicker than 1/4" too because I wanted big, soft cookies. I also used butter instead of margarine, replaced 1/4 cup of sugar with brown sugar and added 1/2 tsp of mint extract with the vanilla because we are all mint lovers in my home. They turned out absolutely perfect! I need to work on my decorating skills though because you can't tell which ones I did vs my 5 year old! This was our first time cutting cookie shapes together and we had a wonderful time making pretty tasty cookies.
This is a great recipe. but caution!... 400 degrees was too hot in my oven. bottoms burned in 5 mins :( so the next batch was 375 degrees and 6 min baking time. came out perfect.

I added 1 tsp. of Almond Extract and some lemon zest. I also rolled out the dough with confectionery sugar and baked them @ 375* for 11 minutes. I baked them on parchment paper, they slid right off. Great recipe!

I followed another persons recommendation and that was to use butter not margarine and 1 cup sugar and 1 cup icing sugar instead of all granulated. Bake at 350 and use icing sugar to flour surface not flour. Amazing! Delicious and everyone loved!

We made these with a few alterations. I used coconut sugar and raw sugar instead of white. I also used the 3 and 1/4 cups of flour, and baked them at 350* for about 8 mins. I super loved the idea of rolling them out on powdered sugar as opposed to flour, and then we made traditional royal icing to decorate them. They’re thick and soft, everything we’ve been looking for in a sugar cookie. Will definitely share! Thanks!

These were great! I made them the first time following the recipe exactly and, like other reviewers, found them to be too floury and overcooked for my taste. I then made them a second time following other reviewers suggestions of reducing the flour to 3C and baking at 350 until no longer appearing wet. 
This is now my go-to sugar cookie recipe. They taste great plain or iced.

Really good recipe- made as is except used 1/2 butter and 1/2 margarine. I decided to make them into Imperial cookies by rolling the dough thin and cutting out small circles, then once baked, put jam between 2 cookies and iced the top. I took them to work - everyone loved them! Thanks for the recipe!
LOVE it soooo much. Simple but yummy.

As written, these cookies are bland and tasteless (I cannot stress enough how bland, it was like the cookie equivalent of water), but with a few changes I managed to make a pretty good cookie that perfectly keeps its shape. I followed other reviews advice and only use 3 cups flour. I used Dark Brown Sugar instead of regular, and doubled the amount of Vanilla Extract. Spreading some light flour on the cutting surface helps keep the cookies from sticking. 10 mins at 350 degrees is perfect, just let the cookies set for a minute on the sheet so they finish through, they will still be VERY soft when first removing from the oven and touching them while still hot will "dent" and ruin the cookie. As long as the surface looks "dry" and some very light browning on the bottom lets you know they're ready to take out, or else they will burn quickly.
Way too much flour. I should have read comments before I made it.
Easy and pefrect
Easy!
I baked the cookies at 350° for 9 minutes. Cooled them a couple minutes on the sheet then transferred them to parchment on my counter. Perfect! The temperature should be updated on this recipe.
These cookies are fabulous! I followed recipe. My grandchildren finished them up within 24 hours! Will make again!!!

I followed the recipe exactly as written. It’s easy enough that my 7 year old and 3 year old twins were able to be very hands on with making the cookies and decorating them. They were DELICIOUS - and I typically don’t like Christmas cookies bc of the texture. These were perfect and the whole family loved them. We will be saving this recipe!
Love it, baking is so much fun!!!
